title: UNEARTH
problem: People risk losing their digital memories and need control over how those memories are shared.
overview: Unearth lets people collect memories in digital time capsules and explore stories left by others.
role: I was the sole designer, conducting interviews and usability tests and developing the identity, wireframes, and prototypes in Figma.
contribution: Research, Branding, Usability testing, UX/UI Design, Prototypes.

sections.title: The project

list: Help people preserve and share personal histories.
Make stories easy to organize and explore across generations.

blocks: Accessibility shapes who can take part in storytelling. It needs attention from the first sketch, especially when designing for different generations.

sections.title: Understanding the user
blocks: Interview participants felt disconnected from their personal histories and unsure how to preserve them. They wanted a simpler way to collect and share memories.
The Sarah persona helped focus the design on preserving personal stories and making them accessible.

sections.title: Design Process
blocks: I tested layouts on paper before building wireframes. The home screen centers on the time capsule collection, with options to create, share, and explore stories.

sections.title: Usability Testing
blocks: Participants valued the personal and educational uses of time capsules. Feedback pointed to simpler interactions and better accessibility as areas to refine.

list: Provide captions and transcripts for audio and video.
Give forms descriptive labels and useful error messages.
Test with people of different ages and abilities.
Refine accessibility based on their feedback.
Add guides, tutorials, and lesson plans.
